questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the culture was somewhat known to me, and that it would be easy to adapt to the culture. The school was at a high level too.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not very easy. Especially finding housing was difficult, and knowing who to contact regarding getting the courses that would be acknowledged by UCPH.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I found some help by the international office at the school, otherwise my coordinator at KU.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very difficult and very expensive to find housing in Los Angeles. I would recommend to live outside of Westwood, to get more of the LA vibe instead of student vibe.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it is doable, and it is easier to find housing once you are there. Maybe get an airbnb for the first few weeks, and then find housing while there. Never sign anything before seeing it in person.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You sign up for courses, and then during the first two weeks of the quarter, you drop the courses you do not want to keep.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I was surprised that there was not more help to find. Or maybe I just did not come across the right people.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It is difficult to get the good classes, since the school prioritizes seniors first, and the exchange students last.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go to UCLA when you have some elective courses to take there. Makes it easier and less stressful to get classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Easier level compared to KU, but more homework each week. Felt like being in gymnasium again.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot of the courses will take attendance, and more of the subjects are just multiple choice, learn by heart kind of teaching.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.answer:

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
Developmental psychology
Cognitive psychology
Culture and human development
Intimate relationships
Dean's honors list

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Culture and human development, it is given by the most amazing professor.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Housing was a lot more expensive than expected. And local transportation (i took buses, but after sundown only uber)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Getting around in a car is less expensive than in DK. Otherwise things are generally around the same price or more expensive than DK.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not do clubs or sports at UCLA, instead I did it in the city.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are numerous clubs and activities at UCLA, I chose not to enroll in any, and instead surf and ski on my own.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to do what you can to get out and explore California. It truly is an amazing place, especially nature wise.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go surfing and skiing and get out of town! California is so diverse and filled with many different kinds of nature and towns.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. The language and somewhat also the culture is known already.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: At first it was difficult to get used to the superficial kindness that is somewhat more in LA than in DK. But after a while and getting to know some people on a deeper level, it was amazing. It can feel lonely to be in LA in the beginning, but once you get past that initial hurdle, it is going to be so worth it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People seem a lot more open to strangers than in DK.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: It is going to be very expensive to live in LA.
